Hi Marta — thanks for the quick report and the HAR/screenshots. Sorry for the interruption this causes. I'm looping in Ben from Platform (cc) and Laura from Customer Success.

Ben — initial look suggests the /activate redirect is dropping the post-redirect state (the crumb/token we set to protect the accept flow). The 403 text matches our guard when the crumb is absent. Can you review the HAR and server logs attached and confirm whether the __Host-accept_crumb cookie is being set on the first response and whether it is being sent on the subsequent POST? Also, if the redirect involves a third-party (Okta), check for SameSite cookie handling.

Marta — two quick things to try while we debug:
1) Open the invite link in a private/incognito window (this avoids possible cookie conflicts).
2) If that doesn't work, please reply with the X-Request-ID you see in the 403 HTML (we log that). That will let us pull the exact server trace.

Thanks for the artifacts — stepped through the HAR + server logs (X-Request-ID req_20261221_9f3b2d). Summary and recommended actions below.

What happened (short):
- The initial invite response (302 -> redirect to our /activate) sets a transient cookie named __Host_acceptcrumb with attributes: Path=/, Secure, HttpOnly, but the cookie lacked an explicit SameSite=None attribute.
- The browser context here is cross-site (Coupa -> our domain) because the invite link is rendered inside a redirect chain invoked by Coupa/Okta. Modern browsers treat cookies without SameSite as Lax by default. In cross-site POST/redirect flows the cookie is not sent, so our server rejects the activation with the 'crumb missing' guard (we were seeing a missing POST form token).
- The HAR shows Set-Cookie on response but the subsequent POST to /activate does not include it — matches SameSite behaviour.

Immediate workaround:
- We can reissue invites that use a one-click token (query param) instead of relying on the post-redirect cookie. That is quick but less ideal for CS policy. If Kepler is OK with this, we can reissue ~20 invites in ~15 minutes.
- Alternatively, ask users to open the invite URL directly from the email (not via the Coupa redirect flow). When opened directly the cookie will be same-site and the flow works.

Permanent fix (timeline):
1) Engineering will change the accept-crumb cookie attributes to include "SameSite=None; Secure" and add reproducible test coverage for cross-site activation flows. Target: patch + deploy to staging by EOD today and to prod tomorrow morning. (JIRA-OPS-1742)
2) We will add a fallback to accept via a one-click token when the crumb is missing so customers do not get blocked while we roll the cookie change out. Target: merge within 24 hours.

Next steps for us now:
- Sergio/Laura, please confirm which Kepler users still need the reissue and whether they can open the email link directly (not via Coupa UI).
- Marta / Okta team, let us know if direct link attempt works; if not we'll reissue invites from our side while we push the cookie patch.

I'll own the rollout and will post a short postmortem after the fix.
